text.p: A group of underprivileged Florida children watched wide-eyed on Sunday when a helicopter crashed in flames as it brought Santa Claus to their holiday party, a local newspaper reported.

But all was well on Monday as Santa -- played by Charles Dhooge of West Palm Beach -- was recovering at home from minor injuries, thanks to the heroism of chopper pilot Donald Lloyd. Although he was doused with fuel after the helicopter went down, Lloyd reached through the flames and released Dhooge, his red and white suit on fire, from the wreckage.

"He literally saved my life," Dhooge told the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel. "I was on fire and trapped inside. Mr. Lloyd had gas on himself but he reached through the flames and released the belt and I fell to the ground."

Even the Christmas party was saved as volunteers gathered the 200 shaken children -- many of them crying -- and told them that Santa needed to get his burned whiskers trimmed. A replacement Santa was found and a new load of toys, gathered after calls to local police and fire departments, was quickly brought in -- with reindeer and sleigh.
